title: Pictographs, Bar Graphs, Double Bar Graphs and Pie Charts
seo_title: Grade 5 Representing Data Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_code: Grade 5: 5.2 Representing data; 5.3 Analysing, interpreting and reporting data
standard_text: Draw a variety of graphs to display and interpret data, including pictographs (many-to-one correspondence), bar graphs and double bar graphs; read and interpret data presented in a variety of ways, including pie charts; analyse data by answering questions related to data categories and data sources.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 graphs worksheets: pictographs with keys, bar graphs, double bar graphs and pie charts. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Use the key and the scale.
key_sub: A pie chart shows parts of a whole.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • In a pictograph, the key tells you what one picture stands for: one picture = 5 learners.
  • In a bar graph, read the top of each bar against the scale.
  • A double bar graph compares two sets of data side by side.
  • A pie chart shows parts of a whole: half the circle is half the data.

Examples

Example

Key: 1 picture = 4 learners. 6 pictures

6 × 4

Answer: 24 learners

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Each picture as 1Use the key.
Reading the scaleCheck what each line on the scale is worth.
The wrong barsUse the legend to find each set.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 5 say about representing data?
faq.a: Draw a variety of graphs to display and interpret data, including pictographs with many-to-one correspondence, bar graphs and double bar graphs, and read and interpret pie charts.
It tells you what each picture stands for.

faq.q: What does a double bar graph show?
faq.a: Two sets of data for each category.

faq.q: When is a pie chart useful?
faq.a: To show parts of a whole.

items.q: How many learners have a fish?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 learners. The Fish row has 2 circles and half a circle: 2 × 2 = 4, and half of 2 is 1, so 4 + 1 = 5 learners.
Each star stands for 5 cups. The Fri row has 6 stars: 6 × 5 = 30 cups.

items.q: How many votes did Yellow get?
items.e: Each square stands for 10 votes. The Yellow row has 2 squares and half a square: 2 × 10 = 20, and half of 10 is 5, so 20 + 5 = 25 votes.

items.q: How many books did Dumisani read?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 books. The Dumisani row has 7 circles: 7 × 2 = 14 books.
Each star stands for 10 points. The Bears row has 6 stars and half a star: 6 × 10 = 60, and half of 10 is 5, so 60 + 5 = 65 points.

items.q: How many weavers were seen?
items.e: Each square stands for 5 birds. The Weaver row has 5 squares: 5 × 5 = 25 birds.

items.q: How many days were sunny?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 days. The Sunny row has 4 circles and half a circle: 4 × 2 = 8, and half of 2 is 1, so 8 + 1 = 9 days.
Each star stands for 10 books. The Space row has 3 stars: 3 × 10 = 30 books.

items.q: How many shells did Amahle find?
items.e: Each square stands for 5 shells. The Amahle row has 2 squares: 2 × 5 = 10 shells.

items.q: How many learners chose soccer?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 learners. The Soccer row has 7 circles: 7 × 2 = 14 learners.
Each star stands for 5 learners. The Walk row has 3 stars: 3 × 5 = 15 learners.

items.q: How many learners chose tacos?
items.e: Each square stands for 10 learners. The Tacos row has 5 squares: 5 × 10 = 50 learners.

items.q: How many votes did Summer get?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 votes. The Summer row has 4 circles and half a circle: 4 × 2 = 8, and half of 2 is 1, so 8 + 1 = 9 votes.
Every star has the same value, so the row with the most stars wins. The Room 1 row has 7 stars: 7 × 5 = 35 cans.

items.q: Which row shows the fewest stickers?
items.e: Every square has the same value, so the row with the fewest squares wins. The Ethan row has 1 square: 1 × 10 = 10 stickers.

items.q: Which row shows the most votes?
items.e: Every circle has the same value, so the row with the most circles wins. The Grape row has 7 circles: 7 × 2 = 14 votes.
The key says one whole star = 2 votes. Half a star is half of 2, which is 1 vote.

items.q: Which row shows 25 cones?
items.e: 25 cones ÷ 5 = 5, so look for a row with 5 circles. The Mango row has 5 circles: 5 × 5 = 25 cones.
20 learners ÷ 10 = 2, so look for a row with 2 stars. The Walk row has 2 stars: 2 × 10 = 20 learners.

items.q: How many learners chose pizza?
items.e: Each circle stands for 2 learners. The Pizza row has 6 circles and half a circle: 6 × 2 = 12, and half of 2 is 1, so 12 + 1 = 13 learners.

items.q: How many shells did Ofentse find?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Ofentse bar ends halfway between 12 and 14, so it shows 13. So the answer is 13 shells.

items.q: How many learners chose tacos?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. The Tacos bar ends at the line for 20. So the answer is 20 learners.

items.q: How many learners chose soccer?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Soccer bar ends halfway between 60 and 70, so it shows 65. So the answer is 65 learners.

items.q: How many learners have a dog?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Dog bar ends halfway between 10 and 12, so it shows 11. So the answer is 11 learners.

items.q: How many learners walk to school?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Walk bar ends at the line for 50. So the answer is 50 learners.

items.q: How many votes did Red get?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. The Red bar ends at the line for 10. So the answer is 10 votes.

items.q: How many stickers does Precious have?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Precious bar ends halfway between 50 and 60, so it shows 55. So the answer is 55 stickers.

items.q: How many days were cloudy?
items.e: The scale counts by 2. The Cloudy bar ends at the line for 14. So the answer is 14 days.

items.q: How many robins were seen?
items.e: The scale counts by 5. The Robin bar ends at the line for 5. So the answer is 5 birds.

items.q: How many Sports books were checked out?
items.e: The scale counts by 10. The Sports bar ends at the line for 50. So the answer is 50 books.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar graph go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 2, 4, 6 … Each line is 2 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 2s. Each gridline is worth 2, not 1.

items.q: How many books did Pieter read?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The column for Pieter ends on the line for 8. So the answer is 8 books.

items.q: Which column shows 3 shells?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Find 3 on the scale. The column for Ethan ends halfway between 2 and 4, so it shows 3.

items.q: Which column shows the most votes?
items.e: The column for Orange is the tallest one. The column for Orange ends on the line for 16.

items.q: How many cans did class 4B collect?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The column for 4B ends on the line for 30. So the answer is 30 cans.

items.q: How many learners walk to school?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The column for Walk ends on the line for 25. So the answer is 25 learners.

items.q: Which column shows the fewest votes?
items.e: The column for Apple is the shortest one. The column for Apple ends on the line for 5.

items.q: How many more learners chose swimming than cricket?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Swimming: 40. Cricket: 30. How many more means find the difference: 40 − 30 = 10 learners.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar graph go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 10, 20, 30 … Each line is 10 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 10s. Each gridline is worth 10, not 1.

items.q: How many cans did class 4A collect?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The column for 4A ends halfway between 20 and 30, so it shows 25. So the answer is 25 cans.

items.q: What does the legend on a double bar graph tell you?
c: The total of all the bars
items.e: The legend (or key) matches each colour to a group, such as green for Class 5A and orange for Class 5B. The source tells where the data came from.

items.q: Why does a double bar graph have two bars for each category?
items.e: Each pair has one bar for each group, side by side, so you can see at once which group has more.

items.q: How many learners in Class 5A have a dog?
items.e: Class 5A is green in the legend. The green Dog bar reaches the line labelled 8. (6 is the orange Class 5B bar, 14 adds both bars, and 2 is the difference.)

items.q: How many learners in Class 5B have a cat?
items.e: Class 5B is orange. The orange Cat bar ends one line above 6, so it shows 7. (5 is the green Class 5A bar, and 12 adds both bars.)

items.q: How many learners in Class 5B have no pet?
items.e: Find the orange bar above “No pet”. It reaches the line labelled 6. (9 is the green Class 5A bar, 15 adds both bars, and 3 is the difference.)

items.q: Which class has more learners with fish?
items.e: For Fish, the orange Class 5B bar (4) is taller than the green Class 5A bar (2).

items.q: Which answer was the most common in Class 5A?
items.e: The tallest green bar is “No pet”, with 9 learners. (Dog has 8. Cat is the tallest orange bar, for Class 5B.)

items.q: How many more learners in Class 5A than in Class 5B have a dog?
items.e: Dog: Class 5A has 8 and Class 5B has 6. 8 − 6 = 2 more learners. (14 adds the two bars.)

items.q: Every learner in Class 5A answered. How many learners are in Class 5A?
items.e: Add the green bars: 8 + 5 + 2 + 9 = 24. (23 adds the orange Class 5B bars, 47 adds both classes, and 9 is only the tallest bar.)

items.q: Every learner in Class 5B answered. How many learners are in Class 5B?
items.e: Add the orange bars: 6 + 7 + 4 + 6 = 23. (24 adds the green Class 5A bars, and 7 is only the tallest bar.)

items.q: In Week 3, how many more cans were collected in 2 026 than in 2 025?
items.e: Week 3: 2 026 has 110 and 2 025 has 90. 110 − 90 = 20. (200 adds the bars, 2 counts lines, and 110 is one bar.)

items.q: How many cans were collected in Week 4 of both years together?
items.e: Week 4: 60 + 80 = 140 cans. (20 is the difference, 80 is one bar, and 14 counts lines.)

items.q: How many more cans were collected in 2 026 than in 2 025, in all four weeks?
items.e: 2 026: 60 + 50 + 110 + 80 = 300. 2 025: 40 + 70 + 90 + 60 = 260. 300 − 260 = 40. (560 adds the two totals, 20 is only the Week 3 difference, and 4 counts lines.)

items.q: Which week had the most cans for both years together?
items.e: Add each pair: Week 1 100, Week 2 120, Week 3 200, Week 4 140. Week 3 has the most. (110 is only one bar.)

items.q: How many more learners biked to school in spring than in autumn?
items.e: Bike: spring 10, autumn 4. 10 − 4 = 6. (14 adds the bars, 3 counts grid lines, and 10 is only the spring bar.)

items.q: Which way to school went down the most from autumn to spring?
items.e: Car went from 10 to 4, down 6. Bus went from 8 to 6, down 2. Walk and bike went up. (Bike changed by 6 too, but it went up.)

items.q: In spring, how many learners walked or biked?
items.e: Spring (orange): walk 14 + bike 10 = 24. (14 is walking only, 16 uses the autumn bars, and 12 counts grid lines.)

items.q: In autumn, how many times as many learners walked as biked?
items.e: Autumn: walk 12, bike 4. 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so 3 times as many. (8 is 12 − 4, which is how many more, 16 adds them, and 4 is the bike bar.)

items.q: Did the same number of learners answer in autumn and in spring?
items.e: Autumn: 12 + 4 + 8 + 10 = 34. Spring: 14 + 10 + 6 + 4 = 34. The same class answered twice. (68 adds both seasons.)

items.q: For which answer is the difference between the two classes the greatest?
items.e: Differences: dog 2, cat 2, fish 2, no pet 9 − 6 = 3. “No pet” has the biggest gap.

items.q: How many learners come by car?
items.e: Car is 2 of the 8 equal parts: 28 = 14 of the pie. 14 of 40 = 40 ÷ 4 = 10 learners.

items.q: How many learners walk to school?
items.e: Walk is half of the pie. Half of 40 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 learners.

items.q: How many learners cycle to school?
items.e: Bike is 1 of the 8 equal parts: 18 of 40 = 40 ÷ 8 = 5 learners.

items.q: What percentage of the families went to France?
items.e: The circle is split into 10 equal parts, so each part is 10%. France has 3 parts: 3 × 10% = 30%.

items.q: How many of the 50 families went to Spain?
items.e: Spain has 4 of the 10 parts: 410 = 40%. 10% of 50 = 5, so 40% = 4 × 5 = 20 families.

items.q: How many learners chose apples?
items.e: Apple is 2 of the 6 equal parts: 26 = 13. 13 of 60 = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 learners.

items.q: 12 learners chose swimming. How many learners were asked altogether?
items.e: Swimming is 2 of the 8 parts = 14 of the pie. If 14 is 12 learners, the whole is 4 × 12 = 48 learners.

items.q: 9 learners chose rugby. How many learners were asked altogether?
items.e: 10% is 9 learners. 100% is 10 times as many: 10 × 9 = 90 learners.

items.q: How many adults chose tea?
items.e: 25% = 14. 14 of 300 = 300 ÷ 4 = 75 adults.

items.q: How many learners have a packed lunch?
items.e: Packed lunch is 3 of the 8 equal parts: 38. 64 ÷ 8 = 8, so 38 = 3 × 8 = 24 learners.

items.q: How many learners go home for lunch?
items.e: Home is 1 of the 8 equal parts: 18 of 64 = 64 ÷ 8 = 8 learners.

items.q: How many learners chose juice?
How many learners chose milk?
How many of the cars are silver?
items.e: Each of the 10 equal parts is 10%. Silver has 4 parts = 40%. 40% of 100 = 40 cars.

items.q: What percentage of the cars are not black?
items.e: Black is 3 of the 10 parts = 30%. Not black: 100% − 30% = 70%.

items.q: Which class has more learners who chose soccer?
items.e: 6A: 23 of 24 = 16 learners. 6B: 13 of 60 = 20 learners. 6B has more, even though its sector is smaller, because 6B has more learners.

items.q: Kyle says, “More learners walk at School A, because its Walk sector is bigger.” Is he right?
items.e: School A: 14 of 120 = 30. School B: 16 of 300 = 50. The sector size only shows the fraction, not the number of learners.

items.q: Which graph is best to show how the temperature changes during a day?
items.e: Temperature changes over time. A line graph joins the readings so you can see it rise and fall.

items.q: Which graph is best to show what fraction of a class chose each school dinner?
items.e: A pie chart shows how a whole is split into parts, so you can see each fraction.

items.q: Which sentence about a pie chart is true?
c: A bigger sector always means more people
items.e: A pie chart is a circle, so the angles add up to 360°. A bigger sector is a bigger fraction, but only more people if the totals are the same.

items.q: In which week were the most salmon counted in 2 026?
items.e: The tallest orange bar is Week 3, at 45 salmon.

items.q: Which year had more salmon in all four weeks?
items.e: 2 025: 15 + 35 + 40 + 20 = 110. 2 026: 10 + 25 + 45 + 30 = 110. The totals are the same, even though 2 026 has the tallest bar.

items.q: How many fewer learners came by car in spring than in autumn?
items.e: Car: autumn 10, spring 4. 10 − 4 = 6 fewer. (14 adds the bars, 4 is one bar, and 3 counts grid lines.)

items.q: Which is a reasonable reason for the changes from autumn to spring?
c: Spring weather is better for biking
The graph uses a scale of 2
Fewer learners are in the class
items.e: More learners biked and walked in spring, and fewer came by car. Nicer spring weather is a sensible reason. The class size did not change: 34 learners both times.

items.q: A graph’s scale starts at 50, not 0. The Grade 5 bar shows 60 and the Grade 6 bar shows 55, so the Grade 5 bar looks twice as tall. Is Grade 5 really twice as much?
c: Yes: its bar is twice as tall
items.e: From 50, the bars are 10 and 5 units tall, so one looks twice as tall. But 60 is not twice 55. Always read the numbers on the scale.

How many bars will a double bar graph of this table have?
items.e: There are 4 kinds of book and 2 grades, so 4 × 2 = 8 bars, in 4 pairs. (4 counts only the pairs, and 2 counts only the grades.)

items.q:
The table shows the books two grades borrowed from the library in one week.
Kind of bookGrade 4Grade 5
Fiction3540
Non-fiction2030
Comics4525
Poetry1015
What should the legend of the graph show?
items.e: The legend tells which colour is which group. The two groups are the columns of the table: Grade 4 and Grade 5. The kinds of book go under the bars.

items.q:
The table shows the books two grades borrowed from the library in one week.
Kind of bookGrade 4Grade 5
Fiction3540
Non-fiction2030
Comics4525
Poetry1015
Which scale works best for the graph?
items.e: Every number is a multiple of 5 and the greatest is 45, so 0 to 50 by 5s fits every bar on a line. 0 to 30 is too short for 35, 40 and 45, counting by 1 needs 50 lines, and 0 to 500 makes the bars tiny.

items.q:
The table shows the books two grades borrowed from the library in one week.
Kind of bookGrade 4Grade 5
Fiction3540
Non-fiction2030
Comics4525
Poetry1015
What label goes under the bars, along the bottom axis?
items.e: The categories go along the bottom, so the label is “Kind of book”. “Number of books” labels the side axis with the scale.

items.q:
The table shows the books two grades borrowed from the library in one week.
Kind of bookGrade 4Grade 5
Fiction3540
Non-fiction2030
Comics4525
Poetry1015
Which is the best title for the graph?
c: Books Borrowed by Grade 4 and Grade 5
items.e: A good title tells what the whole graph shows: books borrowed by both grades. The other titles leave out a grade or the kinds of book.

items.q: Each grid line on a graph stands for 2. A bar reaches the 6th line above 0. What value does it show?
items.e: This is many-to-one: 1 line stands for 2. 6 lines × 2 = 12. (6 reads each line as 1, 8 adds 2, and 3 divides by 2.)

items.q: Each grid line on a graph stands for 5. A bar reaches the 7th line above 0. What value does it show?
items.e: 1 line stands for 5, so 7 lines stand for 7 × 5 = 35. (7 reads each line as 1, and 12 adds 7 + 5.)

items.q: A graph counts by 10. A bar ends halfway between the lines for 40 and 50. What value does it show?
items.e: Halfway between 40 and 50 is 45, because half of 10 is 5. (41 treats the half line as 1, 50 rounds up to the next line, and 4 counts lines.)

items.q: How many cans were collected in Week 3 of 2 026?
items.e: 2 026 is orange. The orange Week 3 bar ends on the line between 100 and 120, which is 110. (90 is the green 2 025 bar, 11 counts the lines, and 100 reads the label below.)

items.q: How many cans were collected in Week 2 of 2 025?
items.e: 2 025 is green. The green Week 2 bar ends on the line between 60 and 80, which is 70. (50 is the orange 2 026 bar, and 7 counts the lines.)

items.q: What does each grid line on this graph stand for?
items.e: There is one line between 0 and 20, so each line stands for 10 cans. (20 is the step between the labels.)

items.q: How many cans were collected in Week 1 of 2 026?
items.e: The orange Week 1 bar reaches the line labelled 60. (40 is the green 2 025 bar, 6 counts the lines, and 3 counts the labels.)

items.q: How many cans were collected in 2 026 in all?
items.e: Add the orange bars: 60 + 50 + 110 + 80 = 300. (260 adds the green 2 025 bars, 110 is only the tallest bar, and 30 counts the lines.)

items.q: Which bar ends halfway between two grid lines?
items.e: The green November bar ends between 10 and 12, so it shows 11. Every other bar ends on a line.

items.q: A double bar graph will show these numbers: 45, 80, 65, 120, 95, 110. Which scale works best?
items.e: Counting by 10 gives 12 lines, so the graph is easy to read. Counting by 1 needs 120 lines, 0 to 100 is too short for 110 and 120, and counting by 100 makes the bars too short to compare.
